newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms but fails to hit $18.52 target.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms but fails to hit $18.52 target.

text.p: IPE Brent edged higher on Friday in a correction to recent looses but failed to hit upside targets.
The July contract was up 13 cents a barrel at $18.45 at 0944 GMT after falling back from an opening level of $18.48.
Dealers said that if it could climb above $18.52, the mid-point of Thursday's trading range, it stood a good chance of making further gains.
Having failed to make that target dealers expected prices to stay in the $18.25 to $18.52 a barrel range until NYMEX begins pit trading later on Friday.
"It's probably not going to do much until the U.S. comes in," said Charles Gray at Prudential Bache in London.
A mildly supportive report from the International Energy Agency (IEA) did little to help the market.
The IEA reported accelerating oil demand growth next year and increased its forecast for the demand for OPEC oil later this year. "Its not as bearish as some people were expecting," said a broker.
The IEA revised downwards its estimate of non-OPEC oil supply in the fourth quarter this year, leaving more room for OPEC oil.
Meanwhile, the physical market for crude oil remains weak with only gasoline in the United States likely to lend the wider oil market any support.
With refineries running flat out in the U.S., traders in Europe saw little chance of sending large quantities across the Atlantic.
"The arb keeps getting hit because of production over there," said a broker who noted the fall in U.S. gasoline prices began soon after the huge Tosco plant resumed production last month.
IPE gas oil was up $1 a tonne at $166.75 at 0938 GMT having briefly dipped below $166 support on Thursday.
Dealers said demand in the key German market remains sluggish and saw a prompt overhang building up in the Mediterranean.
Barges in Rotterdam talked around 75 cents a tonne over the screen.
